title: Defending against a tidal wave of AI attacks with Lakewatch, the agentic security Lakehouse

Reynold. So you'll learn a lot more

any piece of software out there today.
Whether it's open source or closed
source, what used to take nation-state

teams of reverse engineers and hackers

these vulnerabilities, now anyone with

200 million personnel records and

an LLM can put on an attack at a scale
and speed that was previously
unimaginable. That's the world we live
in.
And the only way that we're going to be
successful in defending against this is
if security and data teams work
together.
Let me explain why.
To start, most companies today have a
security operations team that's tasked
with defending them. And this team does
three things. First, they
ingest a bunch of data from a wide range
of data sources.
Think employee laptops, servers,
identity and access
systems, all of that telemetry data, log
data comes into a central server.
Then, they write detection rules on top
of that data. So, these are queries for
potentially malicious behavior. So, for
example, if I were to log in from San
Francisco today
and then a couple minutes later log in
halfway around the world, that might be
a sign that my machine was compromised
or maybe it's just a sign I was
debugging.
So, finally all of those alerts go to a
incident response team, which is a team
of analysts that are looking through
every one of those and investigating
whether this is a
truly a threat or just a false positive.
If it's a real threat, they can take
some remediating action like blocking my
IP address or forcing me to reset my
password.
So, that's what these teams are doing.
The challenge is the tools they're using
are outdated. They typically use a
system called a SIM, a security
information event management tool, and
these systems
don't they're not designed for the scale
of threat that we're facing today.
The first problem is that you can't even
get all your data in. This is a mix of
technical limitation and pricing
problem.
So, what security teams are doing is
they do a number of backflips to reduce
the amount of data coming into these SIM
tools.
For example, they'll throw away data
that's older than 30 days cuz they can't
afford to store years worth of data.
Second, they'll run data filtering
tools. This
filters down the incoming data, taking
away things that are maybe less
valuable. Hopefully, you're not missing
anything by doing that.
And then there's an entire class of data
that today's solutions can't even ingest
and can't consider. These are things
like LLM logs, code, Jira, Slack
messages. This is really valuable
context that would help an analyst
determine whether Andrew was using a VPN
and maybe debugging a service or whether
indeed my machine was compromised.
The second issue is that the process
today is incredibly manual. If you look
at these incident responders, the
analysts who have to determine if a if a
particular ticket is malicious or not,
they were dealing with over 7,000 alerts
a week in 2020. That number has gone up
to over 30,000 alerts a week for a
typical large organization.
And it might take them 30 minutes to
investigate one of those to see, you
know, what was Andrew doing before this
happened? Has he ever logged in from
this location before? What what did he
do after?
And so, you multiply that out, and
already you would need a team of over
400 people to meet the number of alerts
you're getting today. And this is only
going to get harder and harder as we see
more agentic attacks happening at larger
scale and at faster speeds.
So, the reality is that with the tools
we have today,
we don't stand a chance in meeting these
agentic threats. We're dealing with
incomplete data because we can't afford
and we can't scale to bring it in.
We're dealing with humans fighting agent
attackers.
And we're dealing with proprietary data
silos where you can't analyze all the
data because it's locked up in different
locations.
The solution here is a big data
platform.
And that's why we built Lake Watch, the
agentic security lakehouse.
This is built on top of the Databricks
platform, so all of your data is stored
in open formats. We make it very cheap

different ways.
On top of that, you have Unity Catalog,

can automate all of these manual
processes and workflows. And finally, we

teams are familiar with and can use
easily.
And so, the result is that you can
leverage all of your data,
whether it's structured, unstructured,
semi-structured data, anything you need

And then, we can apply agents at every
step of the process. On the ingest path,
we can have the agents automatically
apply ETL on that data, do data

with. If a schema changes, the agents
can automatically correct the ingestion
pipeline to ensure you don't have any
interruption in your data that's coming
in.
On the detection path, the agents can
help author can help author the queries
in detection rules for you.
And on the investigation path, the
agents can automatically investigate
these incidents so that the analysts are
presented with a full case and they can
just verify that the agent did the right
task and recommended the right action.
And the result of all of this is that we
can meet the scale and speed of threats
that are coming in today.
